title: Handball Alley
description: Stradbally’s Handball Alley, built in the early part of the Irish State’s history to facilitate local interest in handball, one of Ireland’s lesser-known national sports

The ruins of a large, medieval house of worship. It contains a fortified presbytery, which is believed to have been constructed in the 1200s for protection during the disputes between powerful local families.
title: Ruined Medieval Church

description:
Stradbally’s Market Square is at the centre of a village that has consistently won titles and
high praise in Ireland’s competitive Tidy Towns competitions for its beauty
title: Market Square

description: The rocks at Stradbally Cove are the remains of volcanic activity from almost 500 million years ago during the Ordovician era. At low tide is a large expanse of fine-grained sand flanked by old Irish Woodland.
title: Stradbally Cove
Ballyvooney Cove
description: A dramatic exposure of Ordovician marine sediments that have been heavily eroded by the sea.

title: Ballydwan Beach
description: A beach with a spectacular vertical cliff made of red sandstone and conglomerate flanked by green volcanic, Ordovician era rocks. The sea stack hides the remains of a 17th century mine shaft.

title: Tra Na mBo Volcanics
description: A succession of volcanic rocks including Basalt and Andestie. Look out for green and blue mineral staining in the rocks here.

title: Miner’s cottages.
description: The remnants of the housing that sprung up to support the 19th-century copper mining boom in the area.
Located in an old miners church, the Copper Coast Visitor Centre features exhibitions, a café and a craft shop
title: Geopark Visitor Centre
Temperance Hall
description: Built in 1842 to tackle alcohol problems in the mining community, The Temperance hall was later used as a famine relief centre and now serves as the village’s Catholic Church.
In the 19th century, the Tankardstown Engine House was a hotspot of industrial activity. The mine shafts here descend more than 400 metres into the ground.
title: Tankardstown Engine House

description: Eroded into a distinctive horseshoe shape. Kilmurrin's cliff side to the east features a massive blowhole formed by undercutting from the sea.
title: Kilmurrin Beach

description: The headland here is made from rocks from the Tramore Limestone Formation some of which have fossils of ancient sea creatures like Trilobites.
title: Dunabrattin Head
Dunabratttin Harbour
description: Dunabratttin Harbour provides boats with shelter from the south west gales.
Kilfarrasy beach is backed with dramatic volcanic rocks formed by explosive volcanic activity during the Ordovician era (over 450 million years ago)
title: Kilfarrasy beach

description: Dramatic erosion of sedimentary and volcanic rocks from the Ordovican period by waves and the rain has shaped Garrarus beach as we experience it today.
title: Garrarus beach

description: The village of Annestown sits atop a hill over its namesake beach where, in the beachside car park, stands the ruin of a 19th-century lime-kiln.
title: Annestown

description: The Anne Valley Walk is a 9km trail through wetlands and farmland that ends at the sea
title: The Anne Valley Walk
Dunhill Castle
description: Perched on an outcrop of Ordovician rocks above the River Anne. Dunhill Castle was once home to the La Poer family, it was famously betrayed during a siege after Lady Power served her soldiers buttermilk instead of beer
Dunhill village was once a port for medieival pirates (who sacked Waterford City on occasion). It later stood against Cromwell’s forces in the 1600s.
title: Dunhill village

description: Ballynageeragh Portal Tomb was built in the 4th century BC and is a typical example of an Irish portal tomb.
title: Ballynageeragh Portal Tomb

description: The Anne Valley Walk is a 9km trail through wetlands and farmland that ends at the sea
title: Anne Valley Walk

description: Dunhill Eco Park is home to local crafts, food producers, and green businesses. During the week a cafe and local craft shop are working.
title: Dunhill Eco Park

description: The name “Kill” comes from the Irish “A Chill,” meaning “the church". The village here dates from the medieval period.
title: Kill Village
Cormorant
description: A cormorant is a large, dark waterbird with a long neck and hooked bill that dives underwater to catch fish and is often seen perched on rocks with its wings spread out to dry.

title: Microgranite
description: Microgranite is a fine-grained, intrusive igneous rock with a granite-like composition, while porphyry is a type of igneous rock.

Basalt is a dark volcanic rock from cooled lava, andesite is a gray volcanic rock with intermediate silica content, tuff is compacted volcanic ash, slate is a metamorphic rock that splits into sheets, and mudstone is a fine-grained sedimentary rock made of compressed mud and clay.
title: Mafic (dark) volcanic and meta sedimentary rocks

description: Rhyolite is a light-colored volcanic rock with high silica content, rhyolitic tuff is compacted volcanic ash from explosive rhyolitic eruptions, and slate is a metamorphic rock formed from shale or mudstone that splits into thin, flat sheets.
title: Felsic (light coloured) volcanic and meta sedimentary rocks

description: Slate is a metamorphic rock that splits into sheets, and shale is a fine-grained sedimentary rock with distinct layers formed from compressed mud and clay.
title: Deep marine rocks
Stitchwort
description: A delicate wildflower with small white star-shaped petals, narrow leaves, and slender stems, commonly found in woodlands, hedgerows, and grassy areas throughout Europe.

Sea pink (also called thrift or Armeria maritima) is a hardy coastal wildflower that forms cushion-like clumps with grass-like leaves and produces spherical clusters of pink flowers on slender stems, commonly found growing on clifftops, salt marshes, and rocky shores.
title: Sea pink

description: Sea pink (also called thrift or Armeria maritima) is a hardy coastal wildflower that forms cushion-like clumps with grass-like leaves and produces spherical clusters of pink flowers on slender stems, commonly found growing on clifftops, salt marshes, and rocky shores.
title: Sea pink
The Copper Coast UNESCO Global Geopark
description: The Copper Coast UNESCO Global Geopark is based around many different locations called “geosites” along the mid Waterford Coast and inland. Geosites either tell a part of the Geological story or combine the human with the geological to make combined heritage
